elements.title: Adrien Nunez (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Adrien Nunez (pictured), despite limited playing time, was more highly paid than some NBA draft lottery picks while in college?

elements.title: Aquilegia daingolica (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that specimens of Aquilegia daingolica were collected in 1906 and 1909, but it was first described as a new species in 2013?

elements.title: Yanou Collart (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Yanou Collart helped Rock Hudson get medical treatment when Nancy Reagan would not?

elements.title: The Man Who Knew Too Much (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that when Alexander McQueen, following years of criticism for over-reliance on runway spectacles, presented The Man Who Knew Too Much, it was criticised for its lack of theatrics?

elements.title: Lars Chemnitz (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Lars Chemnitz was one of the first recipients of Nersornaat, the highest honor in Greenland?

elements.title: Always Happy to Explode (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the principal songwriter of a song on Always Happy to Explode asked listeners to "love it for me, for I cannot"?

elements.title: Daniel Hermann (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Daniel Hermann wrote poems on the inclusion of a lizard and a frog in a piece of amber, the eagle in the coat of arms of Poland, and a child suffering from Fraser syndrome?

elements.title: Allied prisoners of war in Japan (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the harsh treatment of Allied prisoners of war in Japan is well known in the West but mostly ignored or glossed over in Japan itself?

elements.title: a cable TV channel (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that a cable TV channel in the UK was still broadcasting primarily in black and white as late as 1979?
